descriptionHtml:
Case priority: P1 · our extension of a stated behaviour · ours: device clock skew (3.8 names time rules, not dictation).

Suggestion B33 · new · not counted as a bug (was S2): Our own extended check (not stated in the UAT or a ticket AC): No AC/UAT line: OAT-01 and TC-23 do not cite 3.8, and 3.8 names retention, carry-forward, the day roll and 'today' only; TFA-94513's '12 hours idle' is about idle time, not a clock jump

A wrong device clock breaks sign-in and dictation: a 12+ hour jump signs the physician out on reload (the server session is still valid); a clock 70+ s fast makes every dictation fail with 'couldn't start'

Tickets: TFA-94513 in progress; TFA-94423 ready for qa · counts as a QA bug: partly · found on: local

Other cases of the same bug (counted once): OAT-01/S07

Approach · TC-23 Dictation Fidelity · S24 A wrong device clock or another time zone does not change dictation (3.8)

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U9 Dictation behaves the same whatever the device clock or time zone: a phone with a wrong clock, no clock set or another time zone gets the same result as any other device. (UAT 3.8)
  • U1 Dictated numbers (doses, lab values, vital signs) are transcribed exactly: same value, nothing dropped, added or changed. (UAT TC-23; TFA-94423 AC 3)
  • T1 GPT-live is the active dictation engine on every platform (no on-device or native recogniser on phones either, Daniela 2026-10-09), routed server-side, with no API key in the browser. (TFA-94423 AC 1; TFA-94423 latest decision (Daniela 2026-10-09))

Test design technique: Boundary values (boundary) — Sit right on the edge of the rule (exactly on time / a minute late, empty, longest, most) and see on which side the behavior changes.

Given Same setup as S01/S02; the server mints a credential that OpenAI expires 60 s after creation, and the browser checks it against the device clock

When Dictate H-01 (Hospital) and N-01 (Nursing Home) with the browser clock shifted by +50 s, +70 s, +1 day and −1 day, and with an unshifted clock in another time zone

Then Every cell gives the same exact text as the unshifted take, with one gpt-live-transcribe prepareSession row and no 'Live dictation couldn't start' message

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): UAT 3.8: a phone with a wrong clock, no clock set or another time zone shows the same state as any other device (U9); each cell must equal the control under the S01/S02 checks (U1) with the engine attributed (T1). On main liveSession.ts:388 throws 'Expired session' when expires_at × 1000 ≤ Date.now(), so the +70 s and +1 day cells are expected to fail even after the one retry; …

Where it ran: local newspec-c (new Playwright specs); test method PW · Playwright script; lane planned in the matrix: AI check (automated)

S24 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-23.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Triage (2026-10-14): 1 row.

Issue type: New product issue · environment local · tickets TFA-94423 ready for qa; TFA-94513 in progress

On a phone whose clock is 70 seconds or more fast, every dictation fails with 'Live dictation couldn't start' and nothing is transcribed, and a phone a day fast opens on the sign-in screen.

Evidence: allure-results/40bdcb76…: 13/18 pass. With the clock +70 s or +1 day, every take ends in 'Live dictation couldn't start' with an empty box: liveSession.ts compares OpenAI's expires_at (created + 60 s) with the device clock. With +1 day the app also opens on the sign-in screen. A matrix risk predicted this; it is not in the dev report, ledger or knownGaps.

Environment: local — main e02167f → 8b4be94a (10-20), local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane newspec-c.

Test method: PW · Playwright script; secondary: CODEREVIEW · Code review — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on local; Source: newspec-c.
